capture.final_message:
Use the standard description of an induced uniformity. For the inclusion \(i:s\hookrightarrow\alpha\), the subtype uniformity is the pullback of \(\mathcal U_\alpha\) along \(i\times i\). Pushing it forward again gives
\[
(i\times i)_*\mathcal U_s
=\mathcal U_\alpha\wedge \mathcal P(s\times s),
\]
because \(i\times i\) is an embedding with range exactly \(s\times s\). This proves the first conjunct via the general map–comap/filter-range identity.

For the equivalence, prove both universal statements independently:

- Every uniformity has a basis consisting of open entourages: refine any entourage to a sufficiently small entourage and take an appropriate open neighborhood of the diagonal contained in it.
- The coordinate swap is uniformly continuous: write it as the pairing of the uniformly continuous product projections, \(\mathrm{swap}=(\mathrm{snd},\mathrm{fst})\).

Since both sides of the `Iff` hold for every relevant uniform space, combine the two implications and then pair this equivalence with the subtype-filter identity.
